  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Helpdesk API

Rails API-only backend for a helpdesk SaaS. Businesses sign up, their owners verify
email and sign in, and each business has its own users. The frontend is a separate
app that talks to this API over JSON under `/api/v1`.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0, PostgreSQL and the gems in the `Gemfile`.

```sh
bundle install
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql
bin/rails db:prepare                 # creates and migrates the development database
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:prepare  # the test database (a "_test" sibling of DATABASE_URL)
bin/rails server                     # listens on PORT (default 3000)
bin/rails test                       # the suite never touches the development database
```

Outgoing mail is written to `tmp/mails/` in development. Raw inbound mail is kept by Active Storage under `storage/` in development and production (see [Email support](#email-support)).

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none (required) | PostgreSQL connection. |
| `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | `DATABASE_URL` with `_development` replaced by `_test` | Test database. Tests never use the development database. |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Frontend base URL. Used for email links and as the only allowed CORS origin. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for all mail. |
| `HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN` | `support.example.test` | Domain that receives support mail. Each business has `<subdomain>@<domain>`. |
| `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD` | none | Password the mail server uses for the relay ingress. Without it, the relay answers `500` and accepts nothing. |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_DOMAIN`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, — | Production mail delivery. |

## Conventions

- Every request body uses an envelope, e.g. `{"session": {...}}`. Bare JSON is rejected.
- **Choosing a business:** send `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`.
  - Signed-in requests can omit it. The token already identifies the business. If it is sent and does not match, the response is 403.
  - Sign-in, verification resend and password reset use it to find the user. Without it, the email must belong to exactly one business.
- **Signed-in requests:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Lists** take `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, at most 100). They return the records under the plural resource name (`requests`, `tickets`, `comments`), plus `count` (all matches, not just this page), `page`, `per_page`, `next_page` and `previous_page`. The last two are `null` when there is no such page.
- **Errors** share one shape: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "errors": {...}}}`. `errors` is present for validation failures. Validation keys are prefixed `account.` or `admin.` on signup, and `comment.` on ticket replies.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/registrations` | header required | Customer signs up for the business's portal, `{"user": {"name", "email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `user` (role `customer`). The user is unverified and gets a verification email. Then the usual verification, sign-in, profile and password-reset flows apply. An email with a pending invitation is refused with `422`, as if it were taken. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/create` | none | Sign up a business and its admin. Returns `201` with `account` and `user`. The admin is unverified and receives a verification email. |
| `GET /api/v1/portal` | header | Public `{"portal": {"name", "subdomain"}}`. |
| `POST /api/v1/sessions` | header optional | Sign in with `{"session": {"email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `session.token`, `user` and `account`. Unverified users get `403 email_not_verified`. Suspended users get `403 user_suspended`. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/session` | bearer | Sign out this session. `204`. |
| `GET /api/v1/me` / `PATCH /api/v1/me` | bearer | Profile. `PATCH` takes `{"user": {"name": "..."}}`. |
| `PUT /api/v1/me/password` | bearer | `{"password_change": {"current_password", "password"}}`. Signs out every session, including this one. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202`. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"token"}}`. Marks the user verified. The token works once. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202` whether or not the email exists. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets/confirm` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"token", "password"}}`. Sets the password, signs out all sessions and verifies the email. The token works once. |
| `GET /api/v1/account` | bearer | Full account, including `status` and `reac",
  "output_tail": "subdomain>@<HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN>`, for example `acme@support.example.test`. Each request also has a private reply address, `<subdomain>+<key>@<domain>`. Staff replies carry it as `Reply-To`.
- **Ingress.** The mail server pipes each message to `POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails` as `message/rfc822`, using HTTP Basic auth with user `actionmailbox` and the password in `RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD`. A wrong password gets `401`, and a body that is not `message/rfc822` gets `415`. Mail is processed in the request that delivers it in test, so no worker is needed there.
- **Finding the business.** Every recipient at the support domain counts, from To, Cc and Bcc, and from forwarding headers such as `X-Original-To`. The mail is for the business its recipients name. Mail addressed to two or more businesses is ignored, and so is mail that names no business. A cancelled business refuses mail.
- **New request.** Mail to a business's plain address opens a request. The subject is the request's subject (`(no subject)` when there is none, and long subjects are shortened to 255 characters). The first public comment is the message's plain text. An HTML-only message is converted to text, and attachments are not part of it. Text over 10,000 characters is shortened, with a note saying so.
- **Customers.** An existing user with the sender's address in the business is reused, whatever their role. Suspended people are refused. A new sender gets an unverified customer account with a random password, and a verification email. Receiving mail never verifies anyone. The new customer sets a password through the password reset flow, which also verifies the email.
- **Replies.** Mail to a request's private reply address adds a public comment, from the requester only. Mail from anyone else is refused. A reply reopens a `pending` or `solved` request, and an `open` one stays open. A reply that also names the business's plain address is still a reply, not a new request.
- **Staff replies.** A public staff reply on a request that came in by email is emailed to the requester from the business's support address, with the private reply address as `Reply-To`. Replies are threaded under the requester's messages with `In-Reply-To` and `References`. Private notes, status changes and assignments send no email.
- **Duplicates and retries.** A message whose Message-ID was already accepted is dropped when it arrives, however many times it is delivered, so it is not recorded as a second delivery. Only accepted messages record their Message-ID, on the comment they create. A refused message therefore leaves nothing behind, and a later delivery of the same message is processed normally.
- **Automated and list mail is ignored.** That covers `Auto-Submitted` other than `no`, `Precedence` of `bulk`, `list`, `junk` or `auto_reply`, `List-Id`, `List-Unsubscribe`, auto-responder headers, bounce reports and mail from `mailer-daemon`, `postmaster`, `noreply` and similar senders. Mail sent from a support address is ignored too, so messages cannot loop.
- **Refused mail gets no notice.** It is recorded as `bounced` in Action Mailbox's table, which doubles as a log. Nothing is sent back to the sender.
- **Limits.** The sender is identified by the `From` header, which is not verified. Anyone who knows a private reply address and can forge the requester's `From` can add to that request. Mail with no text (for example an attachment alone) is refused, and attachments are not kept on the request.

## Layout

- `app/models/account.rb`: business, cancellation, reactivation window, purge.
- `app/models/user.rb`: users, roles, password rules.
- `app/models/session.rb`: bearer sessions (only token digests are stored).
- `app/models/group.rb`, `app/models/group_membership.rb`: groups, memberships, default groups, and the cleanup when either changes.
- `app/models/ticket.rb`: requests, their status rules, group and assignment. `app/models/comment.rb`: the conversation, with private notes.
- `app/models/invitation.rb`: invitations, their statuses, acceptance and the one-pending-per-email rule.
- `app/models/concerns/single_use_token.rb`: replaceable, single-use tokens for verification and reset.
- `app/controllers/concerns/`: error format, business lookup from header, bearer auth and cancelled-account rules, pagination, list filters, reply parsing, and strict true/false parsing.
- `app/controllers/api/v1/`: endpoints.
- `app/mailers/user_mailer.rb`: verification, reset and invitation emails. `app/mailers/ticket_mailer.rb`: staff replies to requesters on email requests.
- `app/mailboxes/`: `ApplicationMailbox` routes all inbound mail to `SupportMailbox`, which opens or continues requests. `SupportMail` reads one message (recipients, sender, subject, text, automated-mail checks).
- `config/storage.yml`: Active Storage services for the raw inbound mail.
- `config/initializers/helpdesk.rb`: settings from the environment. `config/initializers/cors.rb`: frontend CORS.

  "output": "# Turns mail to a business's support address into a request, and mail to a request's private reply address into
# a reply on that request.
#
# Each message is either accepted or refused. A refused message is recorded as bounced and creates nothing, and no
# notice goes back to the sender. All the writes for a message happen in one transaction, so a refusal leaves
# nothing behind and a later retry of the same message is processed normally. A message that was accepted leaves
# its Message-ID on the comment it created, so a repeat delivery is recognised as a duplicate and ignored.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  # Raised to refuse a message. The transaction it was raised in is rolled back.
  class Refused < StandardError; end

  # What an accepted message did: the request it opened or replied on, and, when the sender is new, the
  # account created for them with the token for their verification email.
  Intake = Struct.new(:ticket, :new_requester, :verification_token)

  def process
    if Comment.exists?(inbound_message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
      log "duplicate of a message already accepted"
      return
    end

    message = SupportMail.new(mail)
    account, replied_ticket = destination(message)
    result = account.with_lock(requires_new: true) { intake(account, replied_ticket, message) }

    # Sent after the commit, so the person is only emailed about an account that exists.
    if result.verification_token
      UserMailer.deliver_safely(:support_verification, result.new_requester, result.verification_token)
    end
    log "accepted for #{account.subdomain}: request #{result.ticket.id}"
  rescue Refused => e
    refuse(e.message)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # Another copy of this message was accepted at the same moment. The unique index on the comment refused this one.
    log "duplicate of a message accepted at the same time"
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    refuse("#{e.record.class.name.underscore} is invalid: #{e.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence}")
  rescue Mail::Field::ParseError
    refuse("the message headers cannot be read")
  end

  private

  # The business the message is for, and the request it replies on (nil for a new request). Refuses mail that is
  # not for exactly one business, or whose reply address does not name a request of that business.
  def destination(message)
    raise Refused, "automated or list mail" if message.automated?
    raise Refused, "sent from a support address" if message.from_support_domain?
    raise Refused, "no sender address" if message.sender.nil?

    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: message.recipients.map(&:subdomain).uniq).to_a
    raise Refused, "not addressed to a business on the support domain" if accounts.empty?
    raise Refused, "addressed to several businesses" if accounts.many?

    account = accounts.first
    raise Refused, "the business has been cancelled" if account.cancelled?

    mine = message.recipients.select { |recipient| recipient.subdomain == account.subdomain }
    keys = mine.filter_map(&:key).uniq
    tickets = keys.empty? ? [] : account.tickets.where(reply_key: keys).includes(:requester).to_a
    raise Refused, "replies to several requests" if tickets.many?
    if tickets.empty? && keys.any? && mine.none? { |recipient| recipient.key.nil? }
      raise Refused, "the reply address does not match a request"
    end

    [account, tickets.first]
  end

  # Runs under the business lock, so two messages from the same new sender cannot both create the account.
  def intake(account, replied_ticket, message)
    body = message.body
    raise Refused, "no plain-text message" if body.nil?

    replied_ticket ? reply(replied_ticket, message, body) : open_request(account, message, body)
  end

  # A reply from the requester, and only from them. Anyone else who writes to the address is refused.
  def reply(ticket, message, body)
    requester = ticket.requester
    raise Refused, "sent by someone other than the requester" unless requester.email == message.sender
    raise Refused, "the requester has been suspended" if requester.suspended?

    ticket.reply!(author: requester, body: body, customer: true, inbound_message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
    Intake.new(ticket, nil, nil)
  end

  # A new request. A sender who already has an account in the business is reused, whatever their role. A new
  # sender gets a customer account with a random password, and a verification email. Receiving mail does not
  # verify anyone.
  def open_request(account, message, body)
    requester = account.users.find_by(email: message.sender)
    raise Refused, "the sender has been suspended" if requester&.suspended?

    token = nil
    if requester.nil?
      requester = account.users.create!(role: "customer", name: message.sender_name, email: message.sender,
                                        password: SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32))
      token = EmailVerification.issue!(requester)
    end

    ticket = Ticket.open!(requester: requester, subject: message.subject, body: body, origin: "email",
                          inbound_message_id: inbound_email.message_id)
    Intake.new(ticket, token && requester, token)
  end

  def refuse(reason)
    inbound_email.bounced!
    log "refused: #{reason}"
  end

  def log(text)
    Rails.logger.info("[support mail] message #{inbound_email.message_id}: #{text}")
  end
end

  def staff_reply(comment)

    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, with: :render_record_invalid

#
# The response holds the records under +key+, plus count (all matches, not just
# this page), page, per_page, next_page and previous_page. The last two are null
# when there is no such page.
module Paginated
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  private

  def render_page(scope, key:, &serialize)
    errors = {}
    page = whole_number_param(:page, 1, errors)
    per_page = whole_number_param(:per_page, DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, errors, max: MAX_PER_PAGE)
    return render_validation_failed(errors) if errors.any?

    count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
    # Past the end there is nothing to fetch. Skipping the query also keeps huge page numbers away from SQL.
    records = offset < count ? scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a : []

    render json: {
      key => records.map(&serialize),
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
  end

  # Reads a positive whole number from the query string. Anything else adds an
  # error for +name+ and returns nil.
  def whole_number_param(name, default, errors, max: nil)
    raw = params[name].to_s.strip
    return default if raw.empty?

    number = raw.to_i if raw.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
    return number if number&.positive? && (max.nil? || number <= max)

    errors[name] = [ max ? "must be a whole number from 1 to #{max}" : "must be a whole number of at least 1" ]
    nil
  end
end

# A business using the helpdesk. Everything else belongs to exactly one account.
class Account < ApplicationRecord
  # Cancelled accounts can be reactivated for this long, then purged for good.
  REACTIVATION_WINDOW = 90.days

  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[admin api app assets mail smtp static status www].freeze

  # Declared before users, so requests and their comments go before the people who opened them, and memberships and
  # groups go before the people they point to.
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :group_memberships, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :groups, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 120 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: true,
            format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens" },
            exclusion: { in: RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS, message: "is reserved" }

  scope :cancelled_before, ->(time) { where(cancelled_at: ..time) }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def reactivation_deadline
    cancelled_at && (cancelled_at + REACTIVATION_WINDOW)
  end

  # The address customers email to open a request. Each business has its own, under the support domain.
  def support_address
    "#{subdomain}@#{Helpdesk::Settings.support_domain}"
  end

  def reactivation_open?(now = Time.current)
    cancelled? && now < reactivation_deadline
  end

  # Cancelling stops ordinary access and signs every user out. The data is kept
  # until the reactivation window closes.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts cancelled more than REACTIVATION_WINDOW ago,
  # along with all their users, sessions, tokens, requests and comments. Returns the number purged.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - REACTIVATION_WINDOW
    purged = 0

    cancelled_before(cutoff).ids.each do |id|
      transaction do
        # Re-check under a row lock: the account may have been reactivated since the query.
        account = lock.find_by(id: id)
        next unless account&.cancelled_at && account.cancelled_at <= cutoff

        account.destroy!
        purged += 1
      end
    end

    purged
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      status: cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active",
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      reactivation_deadline: reactivation_deadline,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end

module InboundMailHelpers
  INBOUND_PASSWORD = "test-inbound-password".freeze

  # Points the relay ingress at the test password for the rest of the test.
  def set_inbound_password
    @previous_inbound_password = ENV["RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD"]

  end

  # Runs the block with environment variables set, and restores their previous values afterwards.
  def with_env(vars)
    previous = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
    vars.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
    yield
  ensure
    previous&.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
  end

  # POSTs a raw RFC 822 message to the relay ingress and returns the response status.
  def relay_mail(raw, password: INBOUND_PASSWORD, content_type: "message/rfc822")
    headers = { "CONTENT_TYPE" => content_type }
    if password
      headers["HTTP_AUTHORIZATION"] = ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials("actionmailbox", password)
    end
    post "/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails", params: raw, headers: headers
    response.status
  end

  # A plain-text message, built with the Mail gem. Extra headers can be passed in +headers+.
  def build_mail(from:, to:, subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.",
                 cc: nil, message_id: "#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}@customer.test", headers: {})
    message = Mail.new do

      to to
      cc cc if cc
      subject subject
      message_id message_id
      content_type "text/plain; charset=UTF-8"
      body body
    end
    headers.each { |name, value| message[name] = value }
    message.to_s
  end

  def raw_message(lines)

require "test_helper"

# Merging a duplicate request into another request of the same customer. The duplicate is closed and points at the
# request that survives. Both views show the pointer, and both can filter for closed requests.
class TicketMergesTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    signup!
    @owner_token = verified_sign_in!
    @avery_token = customer_sign_in!
    @sam_token = invite_and_sign_in!(inviter_token: @owner_token, email: "sam@example.test", name: "Sam")
    @sam = user_in("acme", "sam@example.test")
    @duplicate = open_request!(token: @avery_token, subject: "Receipt download broken")
    @survivor = open_request!(token: @avery_token, subject: "Receipt download broken, again")
  end

  def merge!(source: @duplicate, target: @survivor, merge: {}, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    api_post("/tickets/#{source}/merge", { merge: { target_id: target }.merge(merge) }, token: token, account: account)
  end

  def stored(id) = Ticket.find(id)
  def comments_on(id) = Comment.where(ticket_id: id).order(:id)

  # The fields a merge must leave alone on the request that survives.
  SURVIVOR_FIELDS = %w[status assignee_id group_id priority reply_key origin requester_id subject].freeze

  # --- the merge itself ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "staff merge a duplicate into a request of the same customer, and both come back as tickets" do
    merge!

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal %w[source target], json.keys.sort
    assert_equal @duplicate, json.dig("source", "id")
    assert_equal "closed", json.dig("source", "status")
    assert_equal @survivor, json.dig("source", "merged_into_id")
    assert_equal @survivor, json.dig("target", "id")
    assert_nil json.dig("target", "merged_into_id")
    assert_equal "closed", stored(@duplicate).status
    assert_equal @survivor, stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
  end

  test "agents can merge too" do
    merge!(token: @sam_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @survivor, stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
  end

  test "the surviving request keeps its status, assignee, group, priority and reply address" do
    api_patch("/tickets/#{@survivor}", { ticket: { status: "pending", assignee_id: @sam.id, priority: "high" } },
              token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    before = stored(@survivor).attributes.slice(*SURVIVOR_FIELDS)

    merge!

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal before, stored(@survivor).attributes.slice(*SURVIVOR_FIELDS)
    assert_nil stored(@survivor).merged_into_id
  end

  test "a solved surviving request stays solved, and the merge does not reopen it" do
    api_patch("/tickets/#{@survivor}", { ticket: { status: "solved" } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    merge!

    assert_equal "solved", stored(@survivor).status
    assert_equal "solved", json.dig("target", "status")
  end

  test "the duplicate keeps its own comments, which do not move to the survivor" do
    api_patch("/requests/#{@duplicate}", { request: { comment: { body: "Still broken on Safari." } } },
              token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    old_ids = comments_on(@duplicate).pluck(:id)

    merge!

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal old_ids, comments_on(@duplicate).pluck(:id).first(old_ids.size)
    assert_empty Comment.where(ticket_id: @survivor, body: "Still broken on Safari.")
  end

  test "a refused merge changes nothing, including the comments" do
    merge!(target: 999_999_999)

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
    assert_nil stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
    assert_equal 1, comments_on(@duplicate).count
    assert_equal 1, comments_on(@survivor).count
  end

  # --- the notes -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "by default each side gets a private note that explains the merge" do
    merge!

    assert_response :ok
    duplicate_note = comments_on(@duplicate).last
    assert_equal "Merged into ##{@survivor}. The conversation continues there.", duplicate_note.body
    assert_equal false, duplicate_note.public
    assert_equal @owner_token.present?, duplicate_note.author.staff?

    survivor_note = comments_on(@survivor).last
    assert_equal "Merged in from ##{@duplicate}.", survivor_note.body
    assert_equal false, survivor_note.public
  end

  test "staff write each note and choose whether it is public" do
    merge!(merge: { source_comment: { body: "Continuing in ticket #{@survivor}.", public: true },
                    target_comment: { body: "Duplicate checked.", public: false } })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ "Continuing in ticket #{@survivor}.", true ], [ comments_on(@duplicate).last.body, comments_on(@duplicate).last.public ]
    assert_equal [ "Duplicate checked.", false ], [ comments_on(@survivor).last.body, comments_on(@survivor).last.public ]
  end

  test "a note sent without public is private, and a note sent without a body takes the default text" do
    merge!(merge: { source_comment: { public: true }, target_comment: { body: "Checked." } })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ "Merged into ##{@survivor}. The conversation continues there.", true ],
                 [ comments_on(@duplicate).last.body, comments_on(@duplicate).last.public ]
    assert_equal [ "Checked.", false ], [ comments_on(@survivor).last.body, comments_on(@survivor).last.public ]
  end

  test "a public note on the duplicate is seen by the customer, and a private one is not" do
    merge!(merge: { source_comment: { body: "Please follow the other request.", public: true },
                    target_comment: { body: "Internal only.", public: false } })

    api_get("/requests/#{@duplicate}/comments", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_includes json["comments"].map { |c| c["body"] }, "Please follow the other request."

    api_get("/requests/#{@survivor}/comments", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    refute_includes json["comments"].map { |c| c["body"] }, "Internal only."
  end

  test "a public note counts as activity, a private one does not" do
    survivor_updated_at = stored(@survivor).updated_at

    travel 1.hour do
      merge!(merge: { target_comment: { body: "Private.", public: false } })
    end
    assert_equal survivor_updated_at, stored(@survivor).updated_at

    travel 2.hours do
      merge!(source: open_request!(token: @avery_token, subject: "Third"),
             merge: { target_comment: { body: "Public.", public: true } })
    end
    assert stored(@survivor).updated_at > survivor_updated_at
  end

  test "merge notes send no email, even when public" do
    merge!(merge: { source_comment: { body: "Public one.", public: true },
                    target_comment: { body: "Public two.", public: true } })

    assert_response :ok
    assert_empty ActionMailer::Base.deliveries
  end

  test "a note with no text, text that is not a string, or a bad public flag is refused, and nothing is merged" do
    [
      [ { source_comment: { body: "" } }, "source_comment.body" ],
      [ { source_comment: { body: "   " } }, "source_comment.body" ],
      [ { target_comment: { body: 42 } }, "target_comment.body" ],
      [ { source_comment: { body: "Ok.", public: "maybe" } }, "source_comment.public" ],
      [ { target_comment: { body: "Ok.", public: nil } }, "target_comment.public" ],
      [ { source_comment: "just text" }, "source_comment" ],
      [ { target_comment: [ "a" ] }, "target_comment" ]
    ].each do |merge, key|
      merge!(merge: merge)

      assert_response :unprocessable_entity, "#{merge.inspect} should be refused"
      assert json.dig("error", "errors", key).present?, "#{merge.inspect} should name #{key}"
      assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
      assert_nil stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
      assert_equal 1, comments_on(@duplicate).count
      assert_equal 1, comments_on(@survivor).count
    end
  end

  test "a note over the length limit is refused" do
    merge!(merge: { source_comment: { body: "x" * (Comment::MAX_BODY_LENGTH + 1) } })

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json.dig("error", "errors", "source_comment.body").present?
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
  end

  # --- what the customer and staff see ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "every request shows merged_into_id, null until it is merged, to staff and to the customer" do
    api_get("/tickets", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_equal [ nil, nil ], json["tickets"].map { |t| t["merged_into_id"] }

    merge!

    api_get("/tickets", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    by_id = json["tickets"].index_by { |t| t["id"] }
    assert_equal @survivor, by_id[@duplicate]["merged_into_id"]
    assert_nil by_id[@survivor]["merged_into_id"]

    api_get("/requests", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    by_id = json["requests"].index_by { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal @survivor, by_id[@duplicate]["merged_into_id"]
    assert_nil by_id[@survivor]["merged_into_id"]
  end

  test "a customer follows the link from the closed request to the one that survives" do
    merge!

    api_get("/requests/#{@duplicate}", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "closed", json.dig("request", "status")
    next_id = json.dig("request", "merged_into_id")

    api_get("/requests/#{next_id}", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_equal @survivor, json.dig("request", "id")
    assert_nil json.dig("request", "merged_into_id")
  end

  test "a closed request stays readable, with its conversation, to the customer and to staff" do
    merge!

    api_get("/requests/#{@duplicate}/comments", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ "Receipt download broken" ].size, json["comments"].size
    assert_equal [ "The download button does nothing." ], json["comments"].first(1).map { |c| c["body"] }

    api_get("/tickets/#{@duplicate}", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "closed", json.dig("ticket", "status")
    api_get("/tickets/#{@duplicate}/comments", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
  end

  test "both views can filter for closed requests" do
    merge!

    api_get("/tickets?status=closed", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_equal [ @duplicate ], json["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    api_get("/requests?status=closed", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_equal [ @duplicate ], json["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    api_get("/requests?status=open", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_equal [ @survivor ], json["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
  end

  # --- closed requests refuse edits -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "staff cannot close a request by hand, only a merge can" do
    api_patch("/tickets/#{@survivor}", { ticket: { status: "closed" } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json.dig("error", "errors", "status").present?
    assert_equal "open", stored(@survivor).status
  end

  test "a closed request refuses staff replies, status changes, assignments, groups and priority" do
    merge!

    [
      { ticket: { comment: { body: "Reopening?" }, status: "open" } },
      { ticket: { assignee_id: @sam.id } },
      { ticket: { priority: "high" } },
      { ticket: { comment: { body: "Private?", public: false } } }
    ].each do |body|
      api_patch("/tickets/#{@duplicate}", body, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
      assert_response :unprocessable_entity, body.inspect
      assert_equal "ticket_closed", json.dig("error", "code")
    end

    assert_equal "closed", stored(@duplicate).status
    assert_nil stored(@duplicate).assignee_id
    assert_equal "normal", stored(@duplicate).priority
    assert_empty Comment.where(ticket_id: @duplicate, body: [ "Reopening?", "Private?" ])
  end

  test "a closed request refuses customer replies and solving, and nothing is saved" do
    merge!

    api_patch("/requests/#{@duplicate}", { request: { comment: { body: "Still here?" } } }, token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "ticket_closed", json.dig("error", "code")

    api_patch("/requests/#{@duplicate}", { request: { status: "solved" } }, token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "ticket_closed", json.dig("error", "code")

    assert_equal "closed", stored(@duplicate).status
    assert_empty Comment.where(ticket_id: @duplicate, body: "Still here?")
  end

  test "a closed request cannot be merged again, and cannot take a merge" do
    merge!
    third = open_request!(token: @avery_token, subject: "A third request")

    merge!(source: @duplicate, target: third)
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "ticket_closed", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert_equal @survivor, stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id

    merge!(source: third, target: @duplicate)
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json.dig("error", "errors", "target_id").present?
    assert_equal "open", stored(third).status
  end

  # --- links stay as they were -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "when the surviving request is merged later, the earlier link stays as it was" do
    merge!
    duplicate_comments = comments_on(@duplicate).pluck(:id)
    third = open_request!(token: @avery_token, subject: "The real one")

    merge!(source: @survivor, target: third)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @survivor, stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
    assert_equal third, stored(@survivor).merged_into_id
    assert_equal "closed", stored(@survivor).status
    assert_equal duplicate_comments, comments_on(@duplicate).pluck(:id)

    api_get("/requests/#{@duplicate}", token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_equal @survivor, json.dig("request", "merged_into_id")
  end

  # --- targets that are refused ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "the duplicate and the target must belong to the same customer" do
    kim_token = customer_sign_in!(email: "kim@example.test")
    kims = open_request!(token: kim_token, subject: "Kim's request")

    merge!(target: kims)

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json.dig("error", "errors", "target_id").present?
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "a request in another business cannot be the target, and nothing is saved" do
    signup!(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", email: "jo@globex.test", password: "globex-password")
    globex_token = verified_sign_in!(email: "jo@globex.test", password: "globex-password", account: "globex")
    globex_avery = customer_sign_in!(email: "avery@globex.test", account: "globex")
    globex_request = open_request!(token: globex_avery, account: "globex")

    merge!(target: globex_request)
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json.dig("error", "errors", "target_id").present?
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status

    # And the other business cannot merge this business's request either.
    merge!(token: globex_token, account: "globex")
    assert_response :not_found
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "a target that is the duplicate itself, does not exist, or is not an ID is refused" do
    [ @duplicate, 999_999_999, "abc", "1.5", nil, -4 ].each do |target|
      merge!(target: target)

      assert_response :unprocessable_entity, "target #{target.inspect} should be refused"
      assert json.dig("error", "errors", "target_id").present?, "target #{target.inspect} should name target_id"
    end
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
    assert_nil stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
  end

  test "a merge without a target is a bad request, and so is one without the envelope" do
    api_post("/tickets/#{@duplicate}/merge", { merge: { source_comment: { body: "Hi." } } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal "parameter_missing", json.dig("error", "code")

    api_post("/tickets/#{@duplicate}/merge", { target_id: @survivor }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :bad_request
    assert_equal "parameter_missing", json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  test "customers cannot merge, and an unknown duplicate is not found" do
    api_post("/tickets/#{@duplicate}/merge", { merge: { target_id: @survivor } }, token: @avery_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_equal "staff_only", json.dig("error", "code")
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status

    merge!(source: 999_999_999)
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  # --- assignment cleanup still applies to closed requests -------------------------------------------------------

  test "suspending the assignee clears a closed request's assignment, and the request stays closed" do
    api_patch("/tickets/#{@duplicate}", { ticket: { assignee_id: @sam.id } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    merge!
    assert_response :ok

    api_patch("/users/#{@sam.id}", { user: { suspended: true } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :ok
    assert_nil stored(@duplicate).assignee_id
    assert_equal "closed", stored(@duplicate).status
    assert_equal @survivor, stored(@duplicate).merged_into_id
  end

  test "removing an assignee from the group clears a closed request's assignment, and the group stays" do
    api_post("/groups", { group: { name: "Billing" } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    billing = json.dig("group", "id")
    api_post("/group_memberships", { group_membership: { group_id: billing, user_id: @sam.id } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    membership = json.dig("group_membership", "id")
    api_patch("/tickets/#{@duplicate}", { ticket: { group_id: billing, assignee_id: @sam.id } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    assert_response :ok
    merge!
    assert_response :ok

    api_delete("/group_memberships/#{membership}", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :no_content
    assert_nil stored(@duplicate).assignee_id
    assert_equal billing, stored(@duplicate).group_id
    assert_equal "closed", stored(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "deleting the group clears a closed request's group and assignment" do
    api_post("/groups", { group: { name: "Billing" } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    billing = json.dig("group", "id")
    api_patch("/tickets/#{@duplicate}", { ticket: { group_id: billing } }, token: @owner_token, account: "acme")
    merge!

    api_delete("/groups/#{billing}", token: @owner_token, account: "acme")

    assert_response :no_content
    assert_nil stored(@duplicate).group_id
    assert_equal "closed", stored(@duplicate).status
  end

  # --- concurrent edits ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "a reply that was loaded before the merge is refused once the merge has closed the request" do
    stale = stored(@duplicate)
    merge!
    avery = user_in("acme", "avery@example.test")

    assert_raises(Ticket::Closed) { stale.reply!(author: avery, body: "A late reply.", customer: true) }
    assert_empty Comment.where(ticket_id: @duplicate, body: "A late reply.")
  end

  test "a merge into a request that was closed after it was loaded is refused" do
    stale_target = stored(@survivor)
    third = open_request!(token: @avery_token, subject: "A third request")
    merge!(source: @survivor, target: third)

    duplicate = stored(@duplicate)
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
      duplicate.merge_into!(target_id: stale_target.id, author: user_in("acme", "jo@acme.test"))
    end
    assert_equal "open", stored(@duplicate).status
  end
end

    signup!

    @acme = Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme")

    assert_equal 204, relay_mail(build_mail(from: "Avery <avery@example.test>", to: support_address,
                                            subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.",
                                            message_id: "first@example.test"))
    @duplicate = last_ticket
    assert_equal 204, relay_mail(build_mail(from: "avery@example.test", to: support_address,
                                            subject: "Receipt download broken", body: "Same problem, again.",
                                            message_id: "second@example.test"))
    @survivor = last_ticket
    @avery = @survivor.requester
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  teardown { restore_inbound_password }

  def merge!(merge: {})
    api_post("/tickets/#{@duplicate.id}/merge", { merge: { target_id: @survivor.id }.merge(merge) },
             token: @staff_token, account: "acme")
  end

  def email_back(to:, body: "It still fails.", message_id: "#{SecureRandom.hex(6)}@example.test")
    relay_mail(build_mail(from: "avery@example.test", to: to, subject: "Re: Cannot download my receipt",
                          body: body, message_id: message_id))
  end

    merge!
    assert_response :ok

    assert_no_difference(%w[Ticket.count Comment.count]) do
      assert_equal 204, email_back(to: @duplicate.reply_address, body: "Late reply.")
    end

    assert_equal "bounced", ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.last.status
    assert_equal "closed", @duplicate.reload.status
    assert_empty Comment.where(body: "Late reply.")
  end

    merge!

    assert_equal 204, email_back(to: @survivor.reply_address, body: "This one is still broken.")

    assert_equal "delivered", ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.last.status
    assert_equal "This one is still broken.", @survivor.comments.order(:id).last.body
    assert_equal "open", @survivor.reload.status
    assert_equal "closed", @duplicate.reload.status
  end

    merge!
    email_back(to: @duplicate.reply_address, body: "Refused.")
    email_back(to: @survivor.reply_address, body: "Accepted.")
